significance.justification: Verified true, the conclusion would be that the mid-chain "gap between pivot-decodability and surface-decodability predicts per-example reasoning failure" and that amplifying the pivot representation causally repairs part of that failure. This combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) mechanism and intervention, constraining expected failures across languages and reasoning tasks rather than merely showing that an English-like representation exists; Wendler et al., "Do Llamas Work in English?" (ACL 2024), makes whether latent English mediation has behavioral consequences a substantive unresolved question. It establishes both a phenomenon and a mechanistic bottleneck; a systematic negative result would rule out the proposed pivot-to-surface decoding bottleneck as a general account, although mixed outcomes among its three subclaims would be less decisive. True and false are distinguishable, and after topic substitution the score falls below this level because the broad language–intelligence topic alone supplies neither the predictive gap nor the causal bottleneck.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two named handles: the "DecodabilityGap" as a diagnostic predictor and "Pivot Amplification" as a finetuning-free intervention. The gap is ex ante because it is read at "reasoning-critical layers" mid-chain to predict final surface-language failure, while amplification offers a decode-time action window before the answer is completed. Although the pivot direction must be re-extracted per model, the asserted relation—that a larger gap predicts failure and identifies where amplification should help—would still predict findings after recalibration across languages and several classes of reasoning tasks, making it useful to multilingual-model auditors and deployers as well as interpretability researchers. Topic substitution would not retain this score: the reach comes from the specific forward predictor and intervention, not from the general importance of language and intelligence.
